climate.overview_html: October 2026 closes today as the projected warmest October in the ERA5 instrumental record — approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial October averages, per Copernicus C3S data cited by Dessler and Hausfather, extending 13 consecutive months above the 1.5°C Paris threshold. Ten days before COP31 opens in Antalya, the UN Deputy Secretary-General called on nations not to let “overshoot” become a reason to surrender climate ambition. New presidency initiatives emerged this week: a 35×35 Global Electrification Pledge, an Antalya Compact on Energy Efficient Buildings, and an Antalya AI Pledge. Brazil’s President Lula confirmed he will attend the World Leaders Summit on November 11–12, while the US remains effectively absent following its January 2026 withdrawal from the UNFCCC — the first time a major emitter has stayed out of the framework since the convention entered into force.

items.headline: October 2026 Closes as Projected Warmest October in ERA5 History — ~1.76°C Above Preindustrial; 13th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C Paris Threshold
items.summary: October 2026 closes today as the projected warmest October in the ERA5 instrumental record, with global mean temperatures for the month tracking approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial October averages, according to Copernicus C3S data cited by climate scientists Andrew Dessler and Zeke Hausfather. The figure represents a clear margin above October 2023, the previous record, and would mark the 13th consecutive month with global temperatures above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. The exceptional warmth reflects compounding background greenhouse gas forcing and the record-strength 2026 El Niño. A separate celsius.earth ERA5-based model gives a slightly lower +0.23°C margin over October 2023. The official C3S monthly bulletin is expected in early November.

items.headline: UN “Overshoot Is Not a Reason to Surrender”: Deputy Secretary-General Urges Accelerated Mitigation, Adaptation and Loss-and-Damage Finance Ahead of COP31
items.summary: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed called on world governments on October 30 not to use potential temperature overshoot of the 1.5°C Paris goal as a rationale for stepping back from climate commitments, saying 'overshoot is not a reason to surrender.' Speaking ten days before the opening of COP31 in Antalya, she emphasised that the window to limit catastrophic warming remains open and called for accelerated action on emissions reductions, adaptation investments and operationalisation of the Loss and Damage Fund established at COP28. The remarks reflect the UN Secretariat's framing for negotiations where expectations are being managed downward amid geopolitical tensions.

items.headline: COP31: Brazil’s Lula Confirms World Leaders Summit Attendance for Nov 11–12; UK PM Burnham Also Attending; US Non-Participation Expected After January 2026 UNFCCC Withdrawal
items.summary: Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva confirmed on October 30 that he will attend the World Leaders Summit at COP31 in Antalya on November 11–12, according to Reuters reporting cited in The Print. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is also expected to attend. The US delegation status remains deeply uncertain following the Trump administration's January 2026 announcement of intent to withdraw from the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, making a senior US government presence at COP31 unlikely. Brazil, as incoming host of COP32 in Belém in 2027, has a strong interest in the continuity of global climate negotiations.

items.headline: COP31 Presidency Announces Three Action-Agenda Initiatives: 35×35 Global Electrification Pledge, Antalya Compact on Energy Efficient Buildings, and Antalya AI Pledge
items.summary: The COP31 presidency hosted by Türkiye and co-facilitated by Australia announced three headline presidential initiatives ahead of the November 9–20 summit in Antalya. The 35×35 Global Electrification Pledge targets universal access to clean electricity by 2035; the Antalya Compact on Energy Efficient Buildings aims to accelerate building efficiency standards and retrofit programmes globally; and the Antalya AI Pledge commits signatories to using AI tools to drive emissions reductions and climate resilience. These are voluntary presidential action-agenda pledges that run alongside — rather than within — the formal UNFCCC negotiated text.

items.headline: WMO: Current El Niño May Be “Unprecedented in Strength” — Niño 3.4 Forecast at +3.8°C NDJ 2026–27; SG Saulo: Event “Literally Off Monitoring Charts” Used Over Past Four Decades
items.summary: WMO's updated seasonal outlook projects that Niño 3.4 SST anomalies may reach approximately +3.8°C above average during November 2026–January 2027, potentially eclipsing the 1997–98 record event. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said the event is 'literally off the monitoring charts' used over the past four decades. The OND 2026 GSCU forecast a seasonal mean anomaly of +3.7°C peaking around December. The WMO projects above-normal surface temperatures across most of the globe and enhanced East Africa rainfall for OND 2026, with the positive IOD expected to peak in October and then decline.

items.headline: COP31: Only 77 Heads of State Confirmed for Antalya — A Third Fewer Than COP28; Civic Space Concerns in Türkiye; Campaigners Demand Fossil-Lobby Access Limits
items.summary: With COP31 opening November 9 in Antalya, Climate Home News reports that only 77 heads of state or government have confirmed they will speak at the World Leaders Summit — roughly a third fewer than at the COP28 high-water mark in Dubai. The outlet highlights civil society concerns about civic space restrictions in Türkiye and campaigners calling for limits on fossil-fuel industry lobbying. The reduced head-of-state attendance follows broader diplomatic tensions linked to the Strait of Hormuz crisis. Brazil's Lula and UK PM Burnham have since confirmed, incrementally raising the tally.

items.headline: Pacific Leaders Issue Taku Pakasoa Declaration Ahead of COP31: Commitments on Emissions, Climate Finance and Ocean Protection
items.summary: Pacific island leaders issued the Taku Pakasoa Declaration ahead of COP31 in Antalya, covering emissions reduction ambition, scaled-up climate finance for adaptation and loss-and-damage, and ocean protection provisions. The declaration represents a unified Pacific political position heading into the November 9–20 summit. Pacific nations have historically been among the most forceful voices for the 1.5°C temperature limit and for stronger finance commitments from developed countries. The Planet Brief notes it is a political statement rather than settled negotiating text.

major_events.name: Super Typhoon In-fa (JTWC 30W) — Post-CNMI Passage; Now in Philippine Sea Tracking WNW Toward Possible PAR Entry ~Nov 5; No Philippines Landfall Projected
major_events.status: As of Oct 31: PAGASA’s October 30 4 PM bulletin placed In-fa approximately 2,560 km east of Northern Luzon at 18.9°N, 145.9°E, with maximum sustained winds of 185 km/h and gusts to 230 km/h, tracking west-northwestward at 35 km/h. The storm has completed its passage through the Northern CNMI on October 30; post-passage damage assessment for Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan is underway. PAGASA’s tropical cyclone threat potential forecast through November 5 suggests In-fa may approach the northeastern PAR boundary but projects no direct landfall on the Philippines; if it enters PAR it would receive the name Samuel. A separate low-pressure area inside PAR on October 30 was assessed as unlikely to intensify within 24 hours. Check PAGASA and JTWC for latest advisories.
major_events.impact: CNMI (Oct 30): Damage assessment underway for remote northern islands (Agrihan/Pagan/Alamagan); main population centres Saipan/Tinian/Rota experienced heavy surf and rainbands only. Philippines: In-fa tracking outside PAR, possible entry ~Nov 5, no direct landfall projected currently. Philippines PAGASA monitoring continues; track update every 6 hours.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia/Borneo/Sumatra) — 120,000+ Satellite Hotspots; Hundreds of Schools Closed in Malaysia & Indonesia; Underground Fires Persist Despite Wet-Season Onset
major_events.status: As of Oct 31: Malay Mail reports hundreds of schools have been closed in Malaysia and Indonesia due to hazardous air quality, and that Indonesia has imposed a moratorium on new clearing permits for 66 million hectares of primary forest and peatland and created a new National Peatland and Mangrove Management Agency. The Indonesia–Singapore joint task force announced October 30 is now active. More than 120,000 fire hotspot detections across Indonesia so far this season — approximately seven times the 2025 full-season total. Underground peat fires up to 8 m depth continue burning even as the wet-season transition begins in East Kalimantan. Approximately 40 million people region-wide exposed to elevated PM2.5.
major_events.impact: Indonesia: 333,470+ confirmed acute respiratory cases (7 provinces); ~1.9M ha burned; schools closing. Malaysia: schools closed in multiple states; diplomatic task force with Indonesia active. ~40M people exposed region-wide. CO2 release from peat fires expected to drive measurable atmospheric CO2 spike in November OND data.

weather.overview_html: Super Typhoon In-fa completed its passage through the Northern CNMI on October 30 and is now tracking west-northwestward in the Philippine Sea at 185 km/h, with PAGASA projecting possible PAR entry around November 5 but no direct landfall on the Philippines. Damage assessment is ongoing for the sparsely populated northern CNMI islands (Agrihan, Pagan, Alamagan); main population centres were spared direct impact. The Southeast Asian peatland haze continues, with hundreds of schools closed across Malaysia and Indonesia and the Indonesia–Singapore joint task force now active following October 30’s diplomatic announcement. Meanwhile, today marks the close of the projected warmest October in the ERA5 record — approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial — the 13th consecutive month above the 1.5°C Paris threshold.

items.headline: Super Typhoon In-fa Post-CNMI Update: PAGASA Places Storm ~2,560 km East of N. Luzon at 185 km/h WNW; Possible PAR Entry ~Nov 5; No Philippines Landfall Projected
items.summary: PAGASA's October 30 4 PM bulletin placed Super Typhoon In-fa approximately 2,560 km east of Northern Luzon at 18.9°N, 145.9°E, with maximum sustained winds of 185 km/h and gusts to 230 km/h, tracking west-northwestward at 35 km/h. PhilStar confirms the storm is being monitored outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility. Based on the tropical cyclone threat potential forecast through November 5, In-fa is expected to approach the northeastern PAR boundary but is not currently projected to make landfall on the Philippines; if it enters PAR it would receive the name Samuel. A separate low-pressure area inside PAR on October 30 was also assessed as unlikely to intensify within 24 hours. The storm's post-CNMI track continues westward, potentially toward the Luzon Strait or Taiwan area in the days ahead.

items.headline: Indonesia Peatland Haze: Hundreds of Schools Closed in Malaysia and Indonesia; Underground Fires Unresponsive to Rainfall; New National Peatland Agency Created; Moratorium on Forest Clearing
items.summary: Malay Mail reports that the 2026 peatland fire season has led to the closure of hundreds of schools in Malaysia and Indonesia due to hazardous air quality. Indonesia has responded with a moratorium on new permits to clear 66 million hectares of primary forest and peatland, and created a new National Peatland and Mangrove Management Agency. The article explains that underground peat fires at depths up to 8 metres are completely unresponsive to rainfall or aerial water-bombing and cannot be extinguished until sustained wet-season rains penetrate the full peat column. Less than a third of Indonesia's wildfires occur on peatlands, yet peatland fires produce the majority of the haze. The 2026 season has been driven by El Niño-linked drought and is tracking at approximately seven times the 2025 full-season hotspot total.

items.headline: October 2026 Closes as Projected Warmest October on ERA5 Record — ~1.76°C Above Preindustrial; 13th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C
items.summary: October 2026 ends today as the projected warmest October in the ERA5 instrumental record, with Copernicus C3S data placing the global monthly mean at approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial levels per analysis by Dessler and Hausfather, and a celsius.earth ERA5-based model giving a +0.23°C margin over October 2023. The exceptional warmth reflects background greenhouse gas forcing compounded by the record-strength 2026 El Niño. This marks the 13th consecutive month globally above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. Official Copernicus C3S confirmation is expected in early November.

renewables.overview_html: Two late-October asset deals and a landmark UK planning consent led renewables news. Boralex completed the acquisition of UK onshore wind developer Wind2 on October 29, adding approximately 350 MW of advanced-stage projects in Scotland, England and Wales to its 1.7 GW UK development pipeline. Equitix completed its purchase of TRIG’s 17.5% stake in the 588 MW Beatrice offshore wind farm for approximately £155 million on October 29, lifting its holding to 35% and fully closing out TRIG’s position. The UK government on October 27 granted Development Consent for the 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire — one of the country’s largest solar approvals to date. Earlier in the week, Iberdrola priced $1.6 billion in dual-tranche US green bonds and the EU launched the T-MED platform with up to €4.5 billion in EFSD+ guarantees for Mediterranean renewables.

items.headline: Boralex Acquires UK Onshore Wind Developer Wind2, Adding ~350 MW of Advanced-Stage Projects in Scotland, England and Wales; UK Pipeline Now ~2 GW
items.summary: Boralex announced the completion of its acquisition of Wind2, a UK onshore wind and renewable energy developer founded in 2016, on October 29. Wind2 brings approximately 350 MW of advanced-stage wind projects across Scotland, England and Wales. The deal lifts Boralex's UK development pipeline to approximately 2 GW, alongside 73 MW currently under construction. Wind2's teams are being integrated into Boralex's two UK offices. Financial terms were not disclosed. Boralex was taken private by La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec in August 2026. The acquisition follows Boralex's March 2026 purchase of two onshore wind projects totalling about 58 MW.

items.headline: Equitix Completes Acquisition of TRIG’s 17.5% Stake in 588 MW Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm for ~£155 Million; Equitix Now at 35% Ownership
items.summary: Equitix completed the acquisition of The Renewables Infrastructure Group's (TRIG) 17.5% stake in the 588 MW Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm in Scotland on October 29, for approximately £155 million, lifting its ownership to 35%. SSE Renewables holds 40% and Red Rock Renewables 25%; TRIG has fully exited the project. The transaction was first announced in July 2026. Beatrice, located off the Caithness coast and operating since 2019, is one of Scotland's largest offshore wind farms. The acquisition reflects continued institutional demand for operational UK offshore wind assets.

items.headline: UK Government Grants Development Consent for 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire — One of UK’s Largest-Ever Solar Approvals; Approved Despite Farmland Objections
items.summary: The UK government granted a Development Consent Order for the 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire on October 27, approved as a Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project under the Planning Act 2008. Developer Elements Green submitted the application in June 2025; the examining authority's recommendation reached ministers in July 2026. The site covers approximately 1,765 hectares near Newark, with around 1,025 hectares allocated to solar arrays. The decision was made by Baroness Curran on behalf of the Energy Secretary. The project was approved despite objections from local communities and farming groups over the loss of productive agricultural land.

items.headline: Iberdrola Prices $1.6 Billion Dual-Tranche US Green Bonds — 5.40% 3-Year and 5.85% 7-Year Notes — to Finance US Transmission and Renewable Projects; Book Demand Exceeded $2 Billion
items.summary: Iberdrola priced $1.6 billion in green bonds in the US market on October 27. The offering comprised two tranches: $800 million of 3-year notes at a 5.40% fixed coupon maturing November 2029, and $800 million of 7-year notes at 5.85% maturing November 2033. Proceeds will be applied to US electricity transmission infrastructure and renewable energy projects. Total book demand exceeded $2 billion. The deal closes November 4.

items.headline: EU Launches T-MED Investment Platform — Up to €4.5 Billion in EFSD+ Guarantees for Mediterranean Renewables, Green Hydrogen, Grids and Storage
items.summary: The European Commission launched the Trans-Mediterranean Investment Platform (T-MED) on October 26, providing up to €4.5 billion in EU guarantee capacity through EFSD+ to reduce investment risk and mobilise private capital for renewable electricity, green hydrogen, cross-border interconnectors, energy storage and clean technology manufacturing across the Mediterranean basin. T-MED sits within the broader Pact for the Mediterranean initiative targeting €25 billion in total investment by 2035.

items.headline: Optivolt Raises $32 Million Series A to Scale Module-Level Solar Power Electronics — VXI Capital Leads; Former SunPower CEO Participates; Manufacturing Expansion Planned
items.summary: Optivolt, a San Francisco startup developing module-integrated power electronics for solar panels, raised $32 million in a Series A round led by VXI Capital, with participation from RA Capital, Valo Ventures, Atlas Innovate and former SunPower CEO Tom Werner. The company's Power Balancer dynamically redistributes current among solar cell groups in real time, recovering output lost to shading and mismatch, achieving 99.4% conversion efficiency within the power electronics stage. Proceeds fund manufacturing expansion. Total funding: $42 million. Founded by Thiel Fellow Rohit Kalyanpur.

items.headline: Faria Renewables Acquires 23.1 MW Wind Farm in Boeotia, Greece from EDP Renewables
items.summary: Faria Renewables completed the acquisition of a company owning a 23.1 MW wind farm in Boeotia, central Greece, from EDP Renewables on October 29. The transaction is part of EDP Renewables' ongoing portfolio management and asset rotation strategy in Southern Europe. Financial terms were not disclosed.

science.overview_html: The week’s most striking ML-weather advance: MIT’s Judah Cohen group published a Probabilistic Bias Correction model in Nature (October 14) that effectively doubles subseasonal forecast skill in the two-to-six-week range — the first demonstrated improvement over climatological baselines in this notoriously difficult window. Caltech researchers published a complementary tipping-point advance in PNAS (October 15): a recurrent neural operator predicted a stratocumulus cloud-cover collapse transition within 11 days of the actual event in simulation, more than two years in advance. On foundational modelling, Weber and Kelp (arXiv:2610.22555, October 15) fine-tuned the Aurora foundation model on UKCA chemistry-climate simulations — the first AI system to jointly capture emissions–composition–radiation interactions. Meanwhile NPR’s analysis of Hurricane Isaias confirmed Google DeepMind’s model out-tracked physics-based counterparts while highlighting persistent interpretability gaps, and Copernicus ERA5 confirms October 2026 closes at ~1.76°C above preindustrial — the warmest October on record.

items.headline: MIT Probabilistic Bias Correction ML Model Doubles Subseasonal Forecast Skill at 2–6 Weeks — First Demonstrated Improvement Over Climatological Baselines; Cohen et al., Nature
items.meta: Judah Cohen et al. · Nature (2026) DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11126-x
items.summary: MIT researchers led by Judah Cohen published a machine-learning method for subseasonal weather forecasting in Nature on October 14. The Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC) model learns to identify and correct systematic biases in existing forecast models by training on their historical errors, then applies those corrections to produce improved probabilistic forecasts in the two-to-six-week range. Cohen and co-authors report the approach effectively doubles the accuracy of subseasonal predictions — the first time a model has demonstrably outperformed long-term climatological averages at these lead times. Earlier validation included first place in ECMWF's AI WeatherQuest subseasonal forecasting competition for fall 2025. The two-to-six-week window is critical for emergency preparedness, agricultural planning and energy forecasting.

items.headline: Caltech AI Forecasts Climate Tipping Points Up to 2 Years in Advance — Recurrent Neural Operator Predicted Stratocumulus Cloud Collapse Within 11 Days of Actual Transition in Simulation; PNAS
items.summary: Caltech researchers published a framework for AI-based tipping point forecasting in PNAS on October 15, using a recurrent neural operator (RNO) that detects when a physical system is approaching a critical transition. The method monitors when the model's own predictions about system behaviour diverge from expected physics, flagging an imminent tipping point. In a simplified climate test case — stratocumulus cloud-cover collapse driven by increasing greenhouse gas concentrations — the model predicted the tipping point more than two years in advance, missing the actual transition by only about 11 days in simulation. The same framework was also validated on an aerodynamic test (airflow over a tilting wing). Authors note these are simplified simulations, not operational climate predictions, but the results suggest a promising approach for early warning of real-world critical transitions.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.22555 — First AI Foundation Model for Atmospheric Chemistry-Climate Interactions: Aurora Fine-Tuned on UKCA Simulations; Captures Emissions–Composition–Radiation Coupling
items.meta: James Weber & Makoto Kelp · arXiv:2610.22555 (15 Oct 2026)
items.summary: James Weber and Makoto Kelp submitted arXiv:2610.22555 on October 15, presenting the first demonstration of a foundation model for atmospheric chemistry-climate modelling. The approach fine-tunes the Aurora Earth system foundation model on simulation data from the UKCA (United Kingdom Chemistry and Aerosols) chemistry-climate model. The resulting system captures interactions between anthropogenic and natural emissions, atmospheric composition (aerosols and reactive gases), and radiative forcing — a coupling that conventional AI weather models trained only on reanalysis data cannot represent. The preprint represents an early step toward AI-based emulators that can replace computationally expensive chemistry-climate models for rapid scenario assessment.

items.headline: Google DeepMind AI Model Beat Physics-Based Forecasts on Hurricane Isaias Track — Florida Panhandle Landfall Correctly Forecast vs. Louisiana in Physics Models; Intensity Gap and Interpretability Concern Persist
items.summary: NPR's October 26 analysis reports that Google DeepMind's AI weather model outperformed traditional physics-based models on the track forecast for Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall near Destin, Florida as a Category 2 storm in early October. The DeepMind model correctly indicated a Florida Panhandle landfall while physics-based models pointed to Louisiana. ECMWF's AIFS and DeepMind's model are described by NHC forecasters as the two AI models with the strongest track performance this season. However, AI trailed the NHC's blended consensus on intensity — a persistent gap. Critically, researchers cannot explain why the model makes a given correct or incorrect forecast, a growing interpretability concern for operational use.

items.headline: China Introduces Two Operational AI Weather Models: Typhoon Cloud Pattern Recognition and 4-Hour Severe Convective Weather Prediction Using Fengyun Satellite Data
items.summary: China's Meteorological Administration unveiled two new operational AI weather models on October 30: one designed to interpret typhoon cloud imagery for storm structure and intensity analysis using Fengyun satellite data, and a second focused on predicting severe convective weather — including heavy precipitation and thunderstorm activity — up to four hours in advance. Both models are part of China's national initiative integrating deep learning into operational meteorological services.

items.headline: Nature Climate Change: South Indian Convergence Zone Rainfall Swings to Occur ~Twice as Often This Century — More Intense Rainfall per Event; Major Implications for Southern African Water Security
items.summary: A study in Nature Climate Change reports that climate model projections indicate swings of the South Indian convergence zone — a rainfall-producing circulation feature critical to Southern Africa — will occur approximately twice as often in the twenty-first century compared with the twentieth century, and will produce more intense rainfall per event. The dual signal of increased frequency and intensity has major implications for water security, flood risk and agricultural planning across Zimbabwe, Mozambique, South Africa and neighbouring countries.

items.headline: Copernicus ERA5: October 2026 Closes at ~1.76°C Above Preindustrial — Warmest October on Record; 13th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C Paris Threshold
items.summary: Copernicus ERA5 tracking cited by climate scientists Andrew Dessler and Zeke Hausfather confirms October 2026 is closing at approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial October averages, making it the warmest October in the modern instrumental record. This extends the streak to 13 consecutive months globally above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. The exceptional warmth reflects continued greenhouse gas forcing compounded by the record-strength 2026 El Niño. The official C3S monthly bulletin will be published in early November.

items.title: Boralex Acquires UK Onshore Wind Developer Wind2 — ~350 MW Advanced-Stage Projects in Scotland, England and Wales
items.body_html: Canadian renewable producer Boralex completed the acquisition of UK onshore wind developer Wind2 on October 29, adding approximately 350 MW of advanced-stage wind projects across Scotland, England and Wales to its UK pipeline. Wind2, founded in 2016, also develops solar and energy parks. The deal lifts Boralex’s UK development pipeline to approximately 2 GW alongside 73 MW currently under construction. Financial terms were not disclosed. Boralex was taken private by La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec in August 2026.

items.title: Equitix Completes £155 Million Beatrice Offshore Wind Stake Acquisition from TRIG — Now 35% Owner of 588 MW Scottish Project
items.body_html: Equitix completed the purchase of The Renewables Infrastructure Group’s (TRIG) 17.5% stake in the 588 MW Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm for approximately £155 million on October 29, lifting its holding to 35%. SSE Renewables (40%) and Red Rock Renewables (25%) hold the remaining ownership; TRIG has fully exited the Scottish project. The transaction, first announced in July 2026, completed on schedule. Beatrice is located off the Caithness coast and has been operating since 2019.

items.title: Optivolt Raises $32 Million Series A to Scale Smart Solar Panel Power Electronics
items.body_html: Optivolt, a San Francisco startup developing module-level power electronics for solar panels, closed a $32 million Series A led by VXI Capital, with participation from RA Capital, Valo Ventures, Atlas Innovate and former SunPower CEO Tom Werner. The company’s Power Balancer dynamically redistributes current among solar cell groups in real time, claiming 99.4% conversion efficiency within the power electronics stage. Proceeds fund manufacturing expansion. Total funding: $42 million.

items.title: WindBorne Systems Wins $49 Million US Air Force Contract for AI Weather Balloon Data — 700-Balloon Fleet; Through September 2033
items.body_html: WindBorne Systems, a San Francisco weather-balloon startup, won a US Air Force contract worth up to $49 million through September 2033 for atmospheric observation data from its fleet of roughly 700 long-duration balloons, TechCrunch reported October 12. The contract serves the 557th Weather Wing and 16th Weather Squadron and was awarded without competitive bidding. WindBorne feeds its balloon data into its own WeatherMesh 6 AI forecasting model. The deal is the company’s largest to date, following prior contracts with NOAA and the Navy. WindBorne raised a $37 million Series B in August 2026.

items.title: Finance Earth & FSD Africa Launch Africa Nature Impact Fund — $100 Million Target for Early-Stage African Nature-Based Carbon and Biodiversity Projects
items.body_html: Finance Earth and FSD Africa launched the Africa Nature Impact Fund at the Carbon Markets Africa Summit in Kigali on October 13, targeting a $100 million fundraise for early-stage African nature-based carbon and biodiversity projects that lack capital before first revenue. The first close targets $20 million in 2027, anchored by a £5 million ($6.6 M) commitment from FSD Africa Investments. Fund goals: protect or regenerate 4.5 million hectares of land, sequester or avoid >100 million tCO₂e over project lifetimes, and improve livelihoods for 1.4 million people.
